overview.description: Five Card Stud Lowball is a variant of Five Card Stud where the lowest hand wins instead of the highest. Played with the same dealing structure as standard Five Card Stud (one hole card, four up cards), it uses ace-to-five lowball ranking where straights and flushes do not count against the player. The best possible hand is A-2-3-4-5 (the 'wheel').

history.origins: Five Card Stud Lowball evolved from Five Card Stud in the early-to-mid 20th century as poker players sought low-hand variants. It became particularly popular in California card rooms and American home games as a simpler alternative to Razz (Seven Card Stud Low).
timeline: 1860s: Five Card Stud first appears as the earliest form of stud poker.
Early 1900s: Lowball variants begin appearing in American poker circles.
Mid-20th Century: Five Card Stud Lowball standardizes with ace-to-five ranking.
1970s-Present: Overtaken in popularity by Razz and Lowball Draw, but still played in home games and some card rooms.
history.evolution: The game maintained the simple structure of Five Card Stud while inverting the hand rankings. The ace-to-five system (A-2-3-4-5 as best hand) became standard, with straights and flushes not counting against the playerâ€”unlike deuce-to-seven lowball where they do count.
history.cultural: More common in home games than casinos. Often played as part of mixed-game rotations or as a 'Dealer's Choice' option.

setup.equipment: Standard deck, poker chips, dealer button.
setup.dealing: Five Card Stud format: 1 card face down (hole card), 4 cards face up. Four betting rounds.

rules.objective: Form the lowest possible 5-card hand. Lowest hand at showdown wins the pot.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Ante**: All players post an ante. 2. **First Deal**: Each player receives 1 card face down and 1 card face up. 3. **Bring-in**: Player with the HIGHEST upcard (Ace counting as low) posts a compulsory bring-in bet. This is unique to lowballâ€”high card acts first and must bet. 4. **Subsequent Streets**: Three more cards dealt face up, with betting after each. 5. **Betting Order**: After the first round, betting begins with the player showing the LOWEST hand (pairs count as high). 6. **Showdown**: Best low hand wins.
keyRules: Aces are always low (best card in the deck).
Straights and flushes do NOT count against the player.
A-2-3-4-5 (Wheel) is the best possible hand.
First betting round: Highest upcard must bring-in (Ace is low, so King is worst).
Subsequent rounds: Lowest hand showing acts first.
Pairs are badâ€”you want five unpaired cards as low as possible.
Compare highest cards first when breaking ties (7-5-4-3-2 beats 7-6-3-2-A because 5 < 6).

strategy.basic: Starting Hand Selection: Only play if your first two cards are both 8 or lower with no pair. If your hole card is paired with your upcard, or if you show a high card like a King or Queen, strongly consider folding.
strategy.intermediate: Board Reading: Pay close attention to your opponents' upcards. If you hold A-3 in the hole but three other Aces are showing, your hand is much weaker. Conversely, if many low cards are showing, your medium-low hand gains value.
strategy.advanced: Position Play: In later betting rounds, acting first with a strong low hand can be disadvantageous (you can't gain information). However, with a marginal hand in late position, you can make better decisions based on opponents' actions. The bring-in position (highest card showing) is at a significant disadvantage.
tips: The Ace is your best friendâ€”it's the lowest card in the deck.
Avoid pairs at all costs. A hand with a pair of 2s loses to any no-pair hand, even one with a King.
Watch for 'counterfeited' cards. If you have 7-5-4-3-2 and a 7 is dealt to an opponent, you're now playing 5-4-3-2-X.
Don't chase with 9-low or worse if there's significant actionâ€”someone likely has you beat.
The wheel (A-2-3-4-5) is unbeatableâ€”play it aggressively to build the pot.

list.name: Ace-to-Six Lowball
list.description: Aces are low but straights and flushes DO count against you. A-2-3-4-5 is a straight and therefore a poor hand. Best hand is A-2-3-4-6 (not a straight).

list.name: Deuce-to-Seven Lowball
list.description: Aces are high, and straights/flushes count. Best hand is 2-3-4-5-7 (not a straight). Also known as Kansas City Lowball.

list.name: Five Card Stud High-Low
list.description: Pot splits between highest and lowest hands. Often played with declaration or with an 8-or-better qualifier for low.

list.description: After the fifth card, players may 'buy' a sixth card (face down) for an additional bet. Best 5 of 6 cards play.

list.name: Razz
list.description: Seven Card Stud Lowballâ€”same hand rankings but with seven cards dealt (2 down, 4 up, 1 down). More popular in modern poker.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Razz is seven-card stud; would require phase and deal structure overrides when implementing.

difficulty.easy: Plays too many hands; doesn't understand that pairs are bad; chases with poor low draws.
difficulty.medium: Good starting hand selection; understands ace-to-five ranking; folds paired hands appropriately.
difficulty.hard: Expert at reading boards and calculating 'live' cards; understands implied odds; can execute well-timed bluffs representing strong low hands.

considerations: AI must invert standard poker logicâ€”low cards are good, high cards are bad.
Tracking visible cards is crucial for calculating the probability of improving.
The bring-in position (highest showing) is at a disadvantage and should play tighter.
Pairs are much more common than in high poker and must be avoided.
